title: Rent the City pays to private landlords
question: Where the City is the tenant, how does the rent per square foot compare with the other leases the Board approved around the same time, and which rents jumped at renewal?
finding: The Board approved 126 leases or lease changes since 2014 with the City as tenant, $116,674,873 a year in first-year rent where the title states it. Of the 59 with both rent and floor area, 3 cost at least 1.5 times the middle rent of their period; 2 renewals raised the rent by 8% a year or more over the previous file; 11 were approved after the term had already begun.
how: Passed Board files whose title has the City as tenant. First-year rent and square feet are read from the title. Each lease is compared with the middle rent per square foot of the other City leases introduced within two years either side (at least five needed). A renewal is compared with the previous file at the same address when the floor area is unchanged.
limits: Space differs: a clinic, a hotel used as housing and a warehouse do not rent alike, and location matters more than date. Titles do not show free rent, building improvements paid by the landlord, or operating costs passed through. City leases are negotiated, not bid, and above a set rent the law requires an appraisal, which is not in the title. Leases under the Board’s approval threshold never reach it and are not here. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
